title: Protect data directly into an owned buffer
goal: Protect and recover an application token in caller-owned storage; detect the span capability, retain a byte-array fallback, and discard all output after authentication failure.

selectionNotes: Current framework span route with real IDataProtector capability detection and array fallback.
The valid .NET10 array comparison is preserved in this edition; it is not an additional foundation or selectable span route.

runtime.name: .NET
runtime.reason: The primary route uses ASP.NET Core 11 framework span interfaces.

sdk.name: .NET SDK
sdk.reason: Build a net11.0 consumer with its matching framework references; exact RC2 verification pins are separate.

language.name: C#
language.reason: Canonical current consumer uses C#15; the writer call itself requires no C#15-only syntax.

packageAssets: FrameworkReference Microsoft.AspNetCore.App: Microsoft.AspNetCore.DataProtection.Abstractions.dll and Microsoft.AspNetCore.DataProtection.dll. No additional NuGet package or older-target span backport is qualified.
providers: Real framework DataProtection key ring; explicit AES-256-CBC/HMACSHA256; actual Windows CNG encryptor measured.
platforms: Framework-supported managed host; execution qualified on Windows x64 only. CNG is the measured Windows implementation, not a portable implementation-name guarantee.
renderingModes: Not applicable; synchronous service/console cryptography, no browser or UI.
prerequisites: Reference the ASP.NET Core shared framework; keep exclusive access to caller-owned storage and supply enough capacity.
Use a disposable directory for these test keys, with a separate ring for wrong-key checks. Production key storage/protection policy is application-owned.
constraints: Discover ISpanDataProtector on the actual IDataProtector; otherwise retain the array route. Interface presence does not guarantee a span-capable encryptor or an allocation count.
Input/AAD must not alias destination storage. No concurrent use; copy or consume only successful WrittenSpan before clearing/disposal.
On any failed operation clear the whole destination, including unadvanced bytes; do not consume partial plaintext.
Advanced ISpanAuthenticatedEncryptor is for an existing envelope contract with matching AAD and external key selection. It is not a DataProtection payload or a new algorithm design.
stabilityLimitations: No experimental attribute or suppression is required in these artifacts. RC2 verification is not actual-GA qualification.
No trimming, NativeAOT, other OS/native backend execution, universal zero-allocation, protocol design or automatic token expiry claim.

sources.title: Current span protector and encryptor fallback
Key storage and protection at rest

evidence.scope: Actual isolated framework key rings: token/empty/1MiB round trips, array capability-hiding fallback, wrong purpose/key ring and tampering rejection, input overlap refusal, insufficient capacity and entire-buffer disposal/failed-output clearing. Runtime confirms both span interfaces are absent.

Actual isolated framework key rings: token/empty/1MiB round trips, array capability-hiding fallback, wrong purpose/key ring and tampering rejection, input/AAD overlap refusal, insufficient capacity and entire-buffer disposal/failed-output clearing. Actual framework key encryptor additionally verifies matching AAD and rejected mismatched AAD/tampering on all payload sizes.

humanProof.scope: Real Windows x64 framework crypto executions cover this bounded service buffer goal. No device, browser, external provider or Human observation required; other platforms and actual GA remain unqualified.
